stem: Match the following types of blinding to the appropriate definition.

items.left: both patient and investigator unaware
all parties aware
patient, investigator and analysts unaware
either the patient or clinician unaware of treatment allocation

answer:
The pairings:

DefinitionType of blinding
both patient and investigator unawareDouble Blind
all parties awareOpen Label
patient, investigator and analysts unawareTriple Blind
either the patient or clinician unaware of treatment allocationSingle Blind

From 10 - Body System Organization. Each level of blinding hides allocation from one more party:

  • Open label = all parties aware.
  • Single blind = the patient or the clinician is unaware.
  • Double blind = both patient and investigator unaware.
  • Triple blind = patient, investigator and the analysts unaware.

12 - Evidence-Based Medicine adds why it matters: blinding reduces performance and detection bias, and is critical when the outcome is subjective, less so when it is objective.

stem: Match the following description to the appropriate type of connective tissue.

items.left: Found in the reticular layer of the dermis and most organ capsules (resilient and protective)
Found in tendons, ligaments, joint capsules and has high stress resistance
Found in hematopoietic tissues such as bone marrow, lymph nodes and spleen
Poorly organized fibers found under epithelia, carrying vessels and nerves

answer:
The pairings:

DescriptionConnective tissue
Found in the reticular layer of the dermis and most organ capsules (resilient and protective)Dense irregular connective tissue
Found in tendons, ligaments, joint capsules and has high stress resistanceDense regular connective tissue
Found in hematopoietic tissues such as bone marrow, lymph nodes and spleenReticular connective tissue
Poorly organized fibers found under epithelia, carrying vessels and nervesLoose Connective Tissue

From 06 - Connective Tissue. The keyed mapping matches the note's table exactly.

  • Dense irregular CT is found in most organ capsules and the reticular layer of the dermis; its type I and III collagen is woven into a mat, making it resilient and protective.
  • Dense regular CT (tendons, ligaments, joint capsules) has fibroblasts and type I collagen in rows, for high stress resistance.
  • Reticular CT (type III collagen from reticular cells) supports the hematopoietic tissues: marrow, lymph nodes, spleen.
  • Loose CT sits under epithelia, carries vessels and nerves, and has poorly organized fibres.
note: Key A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I with terms numbered in stem order (existing flag).

stem: Match each description to white or brown adipose tissue.

items.left: Thermoregulation and energy storage for newborns
Multilocular adipocyte
Adult energy storage and insulation
Unilocular adipocyte
Centrally located nucleus
Abundant mitochondria
Nucleus on periphery
Expands up to 4x its size before dividing

answer:
The pairings:

DescriptionAdipose tissue
Thermoregulation and energy storage for newbornsBrown Adipose Tissue
Multilocular adipocyteBrown Adipose Tissue
Adult energy storage and insulationWhite Adipose Tissue
Unilocular adipocyteWhite Adipose Tissue
Centrally located nucleusBrown Adipose Tissue
Abundant mitochondriaBrown Adipose Tissue
Nucleus on peripheryWhite Adipose Tissue
Expands up to 4x its size before dividingWhite Adipose Tissue

From 06 - Connective Tissue.

  • White: the adult energy store and insulator; unilocular (one lipid vacuole per cell), which pushes the nucleus to the periphery; the cells can grow about 4× before dividing, and once divided are hard to clear.
  • Brown: abundant in newborns (2-5% of body weight) for thermoregulation; multilocular (many small droplets), so the nucleus stays central; packed with mitochondria, which is what makes it a heat generator.

The discriminator is locularity: one droplet displaces the nucleus, many droplets leave it central.
note: Key I - C, D, G, H; II - A, B, E, F with I = white, II = brown in stem order (existing flag).

stem: Match the following cartilage types to its location.

items.left: Found in the epiglottis, larynx, and external ear
Found in vertebral disks and the knee menisci
Found in growth plates, ribs and the respiratory system

answer:
The pairings:

LocationCartilage type
Found in the epiglottis, larynx, and external earElastic
Found in vertebral disks and the knee menisciFibrocartilage
Found in growth plates, ribs and the respiratory systemHyaline

From 06 - Connective Tissue. The key matches the note's cartilage table.

  • Elastic cartilage (type II collagen plus elastin) is where shape must spring back: epiglottis, larynx, pinna and auditory canal.
  • Fibrocartilage (types I and II collagen, chondrocytes in parallel rows) resists compression: intervertebral discs, menisci, the jaw, tendon insertions.
  • Hyaline, the most common type (type II collagen, isogenous groups), forms the growth plates, ventral rib ends and the walls of the respiratory tree.
note: Key A-II, B-III, C-I with types numbered in stem order (existing flag).

stem: Match the following bone cell types to its description.

items.left: Bone marrow derived mesenchymal stem cells
Actively secrete bone matrix
Interconnected cellular network within the bone matrix and maintain its calcification
Multinucleated cells which resorb bone and cartilage matrix

answer:
The pairings:

DescriptionBone cell type
Bone marrow derived mesenchymal stem cellsOsteoprogenitor cells
Actively secrete bone matrixOsteoblast
Interconnected cellular network within the bone matrix and maintain its calcificationOsteocyte
Multinucleated cells which resorb bone and cartilage matrixOsteoclasts

From 06 - Connective Tissue. The four bone cells form a lineage plus one outsider.

  • Marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells = osteoprogenitor cells, in the periosteum and endosteum, which differentiate into osteoblasts during repair.
  • Actively secrete matrix = osteoblasts, which also start mineralization with alkaline phosphatase.
  • Interconnected network that maintains calcification = osteocytes: osteoblasts walled into matrix, linked by canaliculi, and mechanosensory.
  • Multinucleated cells that resorb matrix = osteoclasts, the outsider, fused from blood monocytes/macrophages rather than the mesenchymal line.
